research_question: Evaluate hybrid lexical-semantic indexing and reproducible sandboxed workspace architectures for evidence-backed research automation.

sources.title: Hybrid BM25 and TF-IDF Retrieval Benchmarks in Local Knowledge Workspaces
sources.content: Empirical evaluation across 12,400 technical documents shows that combining SQLite FTS5 BM25 lexical ranking with cosine-normalized TF-IDF vectors via Reciprocal Rank Fusion (RRF, k=60) improves top-5 recall to 91.4% compared to 82.1% for lexical search alone. Median query latency remained 14.2 ms on standard CPU hardware without external network calls.

sources.title: Sandboxed Workspace Governance and Provenance Ledgers for Autonomous Research
sources.content: Enforcing path-jailed workspace zones, SHA-256 content-addressed artifact ledgers, and explicit human approval gates before code execution or external publishing reduced unverified artifact drift from 18.5% to 0.4% across 850 automated research pipelines. Atomic temp-and-rename checkpointing recovered 99.1% of interrupted multi-stage runs.

sources.title: Responsible Web Acquisition and Robots Policy Compliance Study
sources.content: Automated research crawlers that validate robots.txt directives, enforce a minimum crawl delay of 0.5 seconds, block RFC1918 private network SSRF targets, and record HTTP ETag headers lowered redundant bandwidth transfers by 63.0% while maintaining 100% policy compliance.

sources.title: Preliminary Blog Note on Lexical Retrieval Speed
sources.content: In a small test of 300 files, standalone BM25 achieved 82.1% top-5 recall with 9.8 ms median latency, though domain terminology synonyms were frequently missed without vector weighting.

claims_to_verify.statement: Hybrid FTS5 BM25 and TF-IDF retrieval with Reciprocal Rank Fusion achieves 91.4% top-5 recall across 12,400 technical documents.
Atomic temp-and-rename checkpointing recovered 99.1% of interrupted multi-stage research runs.
Hybrid BM25 and TF-IDF retrieval achieved only 45.0% top-5 recall across 12,400 technical documents.
Quantum optical storage arrays reduce retrieval power draw by 97% in sub-zero datacenters.
